formulas.name: BD_England_Note
formulas.expression: 'In reaching this decision, the Secretary of State has taken into consideration the biodiversity duty undersection 40 of the Natural Environment and Rural Communities (England) Act 2006, the equality duty under the Equality Act 2010 and the impact on Convention rights as defined in the Human Rights Act 1998, and in particular Article 8 and Article 1 of Protocol 1 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). In particular, the Secretary of State considers, for the purposes of the ECHR, that there is no unjustified interference with the Convention rights of those affected by the decision.'

formulas.name: BD_Wales_Note
formulas.expression: 'In reaching this decision, the Secretary of State has taken into consideration the biodiversity duty in section 6 of the Environment (Wales) Act 2016, the equality duty under the Equality Act 2010 and the impact on Convention rights as defined in the Human Rights Act 1998, and in particular Article 8 and Article 1 of Protocol 1 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). In particular, the Secretary of State considers, for the purposes of the ECHR, that there is no unjustified interference with the Convention rights of those affected by the decision.'

formulas.name: OralHearingNote
formulas.expression: 'The Application was dealt with by the oral hearing procedure. The Inspector held a hearing with the parties on [[oral hearing date]] and also visited the site on [[site visit date]]. The Inspector’s report was submitted to the Secretary of State on [[Inspector report submission date]].'

formulas.name: Point_12_Note
formulas.expression: 'In accordance with paragraph 6(3) of Schedule 4 to the 1989 Act the Secretary of State hereby grants a necessary wayleave in respect of the electric line, and associated equipment, as detailed in the Application. The necessary wayleave is granted for [[15]] years from the date of the grant and is binding on any future landowners or occupiers of the land until the expiration of the wayleave. The necessary wayleave as granted is attached at Annex B.'

formulas.name: Point_6_Note
formulas.expression: 'The Secretary of State has considered the Inspector’s report, which is attached to this letter. The Inspector’s conclusions are set out from paragraph [[insert paragraph number]] of their report, and in paragraph [[insert paragraph number]], the Inspector puts forward their recommendation for the Secretary of State. The Inspector’s recommendation is that [[Insert Inspector recommendation]].'

formulas.name: Point_9_Note
formulas.expression: 'The Secretary of State has carefully considered the Inspector’s report, and all matters set out therein and all other relevant matters. **Insert SoS conclusions** - The Secretary of State agrees with the Inspector’s conclusion that the case for necessity has not been made, but it is expedient to retain the electric line on the property. The Secretary of State also agrees that in light of very little evidence from the Landowner, there is no compelling case that the electric line impacts to any significant degree on the use and enjoyment of the property.'

formulas.name: WrittenRepresentationNote
formulas.expression: 'The Application was dealt with by the written representation procedure. The Inspector visited the site on [[site visit date]] and their report was submitted to the Secretary of State on [[Inspector report submission date]]. '

fields.name: SecretaryofStatesconsiderations
fields.fieldText: Secretary of State’s considerations

defaultValue.stringValue: In view of these considerations, the Secretary of State does not consider the evidence of expediency demonstrated is outweighed by the [[limited impact]] on the use and enjoyment of the property.

Therefore, the Secretary of State agrees with the Inspector’s recommendation. The Secretary of State considers the Application should be allowed, and a necessary wayleave granted for the retention of the electric line at the property.

fields.fieldText: Secretary of State’s formal decision

defaultValue.stringValue: Any reasonable detriment caused by the grant of a necessary wayleave remaining should be subject to compensation either through voluntary negotiation between the parties or through the formal process of the Upper Tribunal (Land Chamber).
